EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows strong aliphatic C–H stretches at 2878/2912/2963 cm⁻¹ and a clear CH₂/CH₃ deformation near 1454 cm⁻¹, consistent with a saturated aliphatic amine rather than an alcohol (no evident OH stretch). A prominent band at ~751 cm⁻¹ and multiple bands in the 900–970 cm⁻¹ region (940, 956) with a band near 1171 cm⁻¹ match known Raman features of triethylamine (skeletal/C–N-related modes and CH rocking/wagging). The weak 2719 cm⁻¹ feature can be assigned to an overtone/combination (Fermi-type) rather than a functional-group stretch. Candidates with OH or C=S/N≡N groups are less consistent (lack of OH/N≡N bands; C=S would typically give a stronger ~1050–1200 cm⁻¹ signature). Supported by CH region assignments (GFQ-003) and overtone behavior (SPC-002).
